production.note: Model years 2017-2022. Start: Ford's specification table is headed '2017 FORD GT TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS'. End: Ford's 5 October 2022 release (source ford-gt-lm-release-2022) is headed 'Marking the final special edition, new 2022 Ford GT LM celebrates Ford's Le Mans winning heritage' and says 'customer deliveries start this autumn with production ending by year-end'. Ford's February 2020 release (source ford-gt-2020-upgrades-release) refers to '2017-19 GT supercars' and the '2020 Ford GT'.

body.note: Ford's table lists the weight under 'Coupe' and 'Seating capacity 2'. No open version was sold.

displacementL.note: 3,497 cc ('Displacement 3,497 cc'; bore x stroke 92.51 mm x 86.7 mm)

fuel.note: Petrol; the European edition of the table gives 'Recommended fuel 98 RON'. Not a hybrid.

transmission.note: 'Getrag 7DCL750: Seven-Speed Dual-Clutch Transaxle', the only transmission.

powerHp.note: Launch rating, model years 2017-2019. Ford release of 25 January 2017. Quote: "Horsepower (SAE) 647 hp @ 6250 RPM". The release text also says: "SAE rated at 647 horsepower and 550 lb.-ft. of torque in U.S. specification". Later increase: for model year 2020 Ford raised the rating to 660 hp (source ford-gt-2020-upgrades-release: 'increased engine power to 660 horsepower', '13 additional horsepower compared to 2017-19 GT supercars'); the 2022 GT LM release also gives '660 horsepower' (source ford-gt-lm-release-2022). The reference year is the launch year 2017; 647 hp applied to three of the six model years and 660 hp to the other three.

weightLb.note: DRY weight, not curb weight: Ford published only a dry weight for this car. Quote (AutoGuide, Sam McEachern, 25 January 2017, reporting Ford's US spec sheet): "the GT's dry weight has been verified at 3,054 lbs". Ford's own table (source ford-gt-specs-release-2017) gives the same figure in kilograms. Quote: "DRY WEIGHT ... Coupe 1,385 kg" (1,385 kg = 3,053.4 lb). New Atlas (source newatlas-gt-specs-2017): 'The car weighs 3,054 lb (1,385 kg) dry.' No qualifying curb weight was found: Evo's specification panel prints '1385kg (dry)' (source evo-gt-2nd-gen-review) and Top Gear's review gives only 'a dry weight of 1,385kg' (source topgear-gt-review-2017); both add rough guesses for a fuelled car ('call it around 1450kg with fluids', 'probably ... getting on for 1,500kg') which are estimates, not specifications, and are not used. This is weight step 4 (a dry weight), adopted on 2 October 2026; the game shows it as dry. Car and Driver, Road & Track and MotorTrend could not be opened; a curb weight from one of their spec panels would replace it.

discrepancies.reason: Unit handling. Ford's rating is 647 hp SAE. Evo's specification panel prints 638bhp, which is what 647 becomes if it is read as metric PS and converted (647 PS = 638 hp); Top Gear prints Ford's number unchanged.
discrepancies.resolution: Use Ford's SAE rating of 647 hp, stated by Ford as the U.S.-specification figure.

discrepancies.reason: Rounding. Ford's metric table gives the dry weight as 1,385 kg, which converts to 3,053.4 lb; the US figure reported from Ford's US spec sheet is 3,054 lb.
discrepancies.resolution: Use 3,054 lb, the figure published for the US market; the two are the same weight.
